review_notes:
I reviewed all 46 lines of the target file. It has one theorem, `exists_scaledPair_basis_height`, and declares no simp lemmas of its own. I also read `DilationPairCoordinates.lean`, which defines `scaledPairDifference`, `scaledPairAssemble`, `scaledPairLayer` and `scaledPairLayerEquiv`. I grepped the OAI tree for uses of `scaledPairLayerEquiv` and `scaledPairAssemble`. Outside its defining file, `scaledPairLayerEquiv` appears only in this target and in two wrapper definitions: `dilationPairLayerEquiv` in DilationPairFiltration.lean and in MultidegreeDilationPair.lean. Neither wrapper unfolds it in `simp`. So the target is currently the only proof that must look inside `scaledPairLayerEquiv` through the simplifier.

The one simp-interface problem I found is that the target proof has to unfold `scaledPairLayerEquiv` and `scaledPairAssemble`. This is because the defining file has no apply/projection simp lemmas for either. The fix belongs in the imported file, but the cost shows up here.

The other simp calls look fine. `simpa only [map_zero, Finsupp.zero_apply]`, `simpa only [Nat.mul_comm K H]` and `simpa only [c', Basis.reindex_apply]` use standard canonical lemmas with no competing rules or cycles. I did not run Lean, so I cannot confirm that the proposed lemmas make the simplified calls close without changes. I am not claiming any simp failure was observed.

findings.problem: To simplify expressions like `((scaledPairLayerEquiv P Q hQP q) (a.prod b (Sum.inl j))).val.1` to the desired normal form `(a j : L) + q • 0` (and later `(a j : L)`), both `simp` calls (lines 31 and 36) must unfold two definitions. The first is `scaledPairLayerEquiv`, a `LinearEquiv` built with `where` (toFun/invFun/left_inv/right_inv/map_add'/map_smul' fields). The second is `scaledPairAssemble`. This happens because the imported interface has no simp lemma giving the coercion or projections of `scaledPairLayerEquiv` applied to an element. `scaledPairAssemble` also has no `_fst`/`_snd` lemmas. The only simp lemmas next to them are `scaledPairDifference_apply`, `scaledPairDifference_assemble` and `mem_scaledPairLayer`. Unfolding the whole structure exposes its proof fields to the simplifier. It also makes the proof depend on how the equivalence is implemented rather than on what it does.
findings.proposed_change:
In `OAI/Combinatorics/Progressions/Geometry/DilationPairCoordinates.lean`, add canonical simp lemmas (all `rfl`):

```lean
@[simp] theorem scaledPairAssemble_fst (q : ℚ) (u v : L) : (scaledPairAssemble q u v).1 = u + q • v := rfl
@[simp] theorem scaledPairAssemble_snd (q : ℚ) (u v : L) : (scaledPairAssemble q u v).2 = v := rfl
@[simp] theorem coe_scaledPairLayerEquiv_apply (P Q : Submodule ℚ L) (hQP : Q ≤ P) (q : ℚ) (x : Q × P) :
    ((scaledPairLayerEquiv P Q hQP q x : scaledPairLayer P Q q) : L × L) = scaledPairAssemble q x.1 x.2 := rfl
```

Alternatively, tag `scaledPairLayerEquiv` with `@[simps apply]`. Then, in the target, replace the two unfolding calls with `simpa [c, Basis.prod_apply] using …` and `simpa [c, Basis.prod_apply, smul_eq_mul] using …`, removing `scaledPairLayerEquiv, scaledPairAssemble` from the simp sets.
findings.benefit: The simp calls in this proof would rewrite through a stable, documented interface (`coe ∘ scaledPairLayerEquiv = scaledPairAssemble`, then component lemmas) instead of unfolding a `LinearEquiv` structure. That makes them less sensitive to changes in how the equivalence is implemented, and simp no longer has to work through the structure's proof fields. The wrapper definitions `dilationPairLayerEquiv` in DilationPairFiltration.lean and MultidegreeDilationPair.lean are defined as `scaledPairLayerEquiv`. Any future proof that unfolds them would get the same projection lemmas instead of having to unfold this definition again.
